hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Military Sites in Iran for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The U.S. military carried out strikes on military targets in southern Iran, marking the second such attack in three days as a fragile cease-fire remains under threat.

The strikes targeted a military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city in southern Iran, according to U.S. military officials. American forces also shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones and hit a drone ground-control station. A U.S. official said the attacks were conducted in self-defense.

Bandar Abbas sits along the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil shipments. The renewed military action sent oil prices higher as markets responded to fears of disruption in the strategic passage.

The strikes come as diplomatic efforts to establish a cease-fire hang in the balance. The U.S. and Iran have been engaged in negotiations, though the latest military exchange threatens to derail those talks. President Trump said Iran was "negotiating on fumes," suggesting the country's bargaining position has weakened.

The four attack drones destroyed by U.S. forces were launched by Iran before being intercepted. Officials characterized the drones and the ground-control station as imminent threats that justified the defensive strikes.

This marks an escalation in military tensions between the two countries over recent days. The previous U.S. strikes occurred just three days earlier, and officials have indicated that remaining military targets in Iran present more challenging and complicated scenarios for potential future action.

The cease-fire, described as fragile by multiple sources, now faces increased uncertainty following this second round of strikes. The military actions occurred even as diplomatic channels remained open between Washington and Tehran.

The situation in the Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern for international observers. Any prolonged disruption to shipping through the narrow passage could have significant implications for global energy markets and supply chains that depend on Middle Eastern oil exports.

cards.headline: US strikes Iran military site, shoots down four drones
cards.body:
The US military launched strikes against a military facility in Bandar Abbas while also intercepting four Iranian attack drones during the operation, according to military statements.

Bandar Abbas, located on Iran's southern coast near the Strait of Hormuz, hosts significant Iranian naval operations and serves as a strategic port city. The US military confirmed the operation but provided limited details about the timing or specific targets involved.

The strikes occur as tensions between Washington and Tehran remain elevated. Negotiations are underway, with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi indicating that a counterproposal on nuclear matters could be ready within days. President Trump has set a 10 to 15-day deadline for Iran to reach a deal on its nuclear program, warning of "really bad things" if negotiations fail.

Trump indicated Friday that he is considering limited military strikes to pressure Iran into making concessions. "I guess I can say I am considering it," he told reporters when asked about a limited strike option. He added that Iran should "negotiate a fair deal."

The military buildup reflects heightened US activity in the region. Trump has ordered a massive increase in naval forces in the Middle East, including repositioning of aircraft carriers and other warships. According to US officials, military planning has advanced significantly, with options under consideration ranging from targeting specific individuals to pursuing leadership changes in Tehran.

Iran's nuclear program expanded after Trump withdrew from an international agreement during his first term. Israel led a military campaign against Iran in June 2025, which the US joined, though the campaign's long-term impact on Tehran's nuclear ambitions remains unclear.

Araghchi rejected the notion that military action can resolve Iran's nuclear program. "That has been tested last year. There were huge attacks on our facilities, they killed and assassinated our scientists, but they couldn't kill our nuclear programme," he said during discussions with Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Geneva this week.

During Geneva talks, both sides discussed principles for a potential agreement. Araghchi stated that discussions focused on ensuring "Iran's nuclear programme, including enrichment, is peaceful and would remain peaceful forever." He noted that Iran did not offer to suspend enrichment and the US did not demand zero enrichment.

A White House official responded by reiterating that "the president has been clear that Iran cannot have nuclear weapons or the capacity to build them, and that they cannot enrich uranium."

Trump also stated Saturday that a potential agreement would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's critical shipping chokepoints through which approximately one-fifth of global oil passes daily.

The UN has expressed concerns about heightened rhetoric and increased military activities in the region.

cards.headline: U.S. military shoots down Iranian drones, strikes launch site amid peace talks
cards.body:
The U.S. military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas on Wednesday, according to U.S. Central Command. The Iranian drones had targeted a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz before American forces destroyed them. U.S. forces then attacked the Iranian drone-launching unit on the ground in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast.

"These actions were measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire," Central Command said in a statement about the military response.

This represents the second military clash between U.S. and Iranian forces within 48 hours. The timing complicates ongoing diplomatic efforts between the two nations. Earlier in the week, U.S. military forces also shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone that approached the Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea. An F-35C fighter jet conducted that operation in self-defense to protect the carrier and its personnel, according to Navy Captain Tim Hawkins at Central Command.

In a separate incident on Tuesday, the Iranian Revolutionary Guards harassed a U.S.-flagged merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Two IRGC boats and an Iranian Mohajer drone approached the M/V Stena Imperative at high speeds and threatened to seize the tanker, Hawkins said.

The military escalations stand in sharp contrast to diplomatic movements. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian announced that he had instructed the country's foreign minister to pursue negotiations with the United States. This marked a significant shift for the reformist leader and suggested support from Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei for talks, which the cleric had previously rejected.

A Trump envoy plans to hold talks with Iranian officials this week despite the drone incident, according to White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt. However, Iran's foreign ministry said consultations were still underway about the meeting location, with reports indicating Tehran preferred Oman over Turkey and wanted discussions limited to nuclear-related issues.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical waterway for global oil shipments, making any military activity in the region significant for international commerce. The narrow passage between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman has repeatedly served as a flashpoint for U.S.-Iran tensions.

The continued military exchanges raise questions about the viability of peace negotiations. President Trump's recent statements at a Cabinet meeting suggested he was maintaining maximum demands on Iran, differing from his weekend comments that an agreement was close to completion. Trump has also accused Iran of attempting to delay negotiations until November's midterm elections in hopes of securing better terms.

Neither side has publicly detailed specific terms under discussion or provided clear indications of how close the parties are to reaching an agreement.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases were reported in the capital Kampala.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak in the neighboring country intensifies. Suspected cases in the DRC have surpassed 900, with 119 suspected deaths reported, according to the country's ministry of communication. The World Health Organization has deemed the outbreak poses a "very high" risk for the DRC, though the risk of global spread remains low.

Seven confirmed cases of Ebola have been identified in Kampala, Uganda's capital. Ugandan health officials say the country has implemented robust disease surveillance systems to monitor and respond to the outbreak. International airlines have been instructed to follow safety protocols as the virus spreads in the region.

cards.headline: Paper mill disaster in Washington state may be deadliest industrial accident in modern state history
cards.teaser: Two people are confirmed dead and nine remain missing after a chemical vat ruptured at a Longview paper mill.
cards.body:
Two people have died and nine others are missing and presumed dead following a tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview on Tuesday morning. One person died after being transported to the hospital following the disaster.

Washington's governor has characterized the incident as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. Fire department officials have shifted operations from rescue to recovery as they continue searching for the missing workers.

cards.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
cards.body:
A court ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address compliance with tariff refunds, signaling new concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay $166 billion owed from tariffs a court ruled were imposed illegally.

The demand for the customs chief to appear in person represented a departure from typical court proceedings and suggested judicial frustration with the pace or completeness of the refund process. The full $166 billion figure represents tariffs collected under policies that courts determined violated legal requirements.

The hearing will focus on whether the administration has taken adequate steps to comply with court orders requiring the tariffs to be refunded. The timeline for repayment and the mechanisms being used to return the funds to affected parties remain under judicial scrutiny.

The case centers on tariffs the Trump administration collected but that courts later found to be illegally imposed. The $166 billion total reflects the cumulative amount collected under those policies before courts invalidated them.

Judges typically do not require cabinet-level officials or agency heads to appear personally unless standard compliance mechanisms have failed or proven inadequate. The order for the customs chief to attend the hearing indicates the court may view current efforts as insufficient.

The refund process involves identifying who paid the tariffs, calculating refund amounts, and distributing payments. Delays or complications in any of these steps could trigger the kind of judicial intervention represented by this hearing order.

The appearance requirement puts direct pressure on the administration to demonstrate concrete progress on refunds. Courts have broad authority to enforce their orders, including through contempt findings or additional remedial measures if compliance remains lacking.

The customs chief will need to provide the court with detailed information about refund status, including how many claims have been processed, how much money has been returned, and what obstacles have slowed the process. The hearing represents a significant escalation in judicial oversight of the refund effort.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million Polymarket profit
cards.body:
Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million betting on Polymarket. The engineer placed wagers totaling over $2.7 million on outcomes related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, according to the complaint.

The charges involve bets the engineer placed using knowledge he gained through his position at the company. Polymarket is a prediction market platform where users bet on the outcomes of real-world events. The platform has grown in popularity for wagering on everything from election results to corporate announcements.

The case marks a new frontier in insider trading enforcement, extending traditional securities law to prediction markets. Prosecutors allege the engineer used confidential information about Google's annual Year in Search campaign to place profitable bets on related outcomes before the information became public.

The Year in Search campaign is Google's annual roundup of the most popular search queries and trends. The timing and content of the campaign could provide betting advantages to someone with advance knowledge of the results or announcement details.

The engineer risked a total of $2.7 million across multiple wagers, ultimately profiting $1.2 million from the trades. The complaint does not specify how many individual bets were placed or over what time period.

Insider trading laws traditionally apply to securities like stocks and bonds, but prosecutors have increasingly applied them to other markets where material nonpublic information could provide an unfair advantage. Prediction markets have faced regulatory scrutiny over whether they constitute illegal gambling or unregulated securities trading.

Polymarket operates using cryptocurrency and has attracted millions in trading volume on high-profile events. The platform faced regulatory action from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in 2022 but continued operating with restrictions on U.S. users.

The charges could set precedent for how insider trading laws apply to prediction markets and what types of corporate information are protected. Google has not commented on the case or the engineer's employment status.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League in Glasner's final match
cards.body:
Crystal Palace secured their first major European trophy by defeating Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in the second half, delivering Oliver Glasner a perfect send-off in his last match as manager.

The victory proved especially significant for Palace, who had been denied a place in this season's Europa League despite winning the FA Cup last year. UEFA had ruled that John Textor held a controlling interest in both Palace and Lyon, breaching multi-club ownership regulations. By winning the Conference League, Palace have secured the Europa League spot that should have been theirs.

Glasner's departure marks the end of a remarkable 12-month period in which he has won three trophies with the club. Along with the Conference League title, he guided Palace to both the FA Cup and Community Shield. The Austrian also won the Europa League with Eintracht Frankfurt in 2022, cementing his status as one of the club's greatest managers.

Before the final, Glasner addressed his players after they held a farewell party for him. He explained his hope that winning would allow them to experience European football at the level they deserved. "The best thing would be winning tomorrow because then the players would be in the Europa League next year and then we get what we should have got this year," Glasner said. He expressed his wish to watch them compete in the Europa League next season, confident they could succeed there too.

Club captain Dean Henderson praised Glasner's impact, describing his departure as "a huge miss." The goalkeeper noted that the manager had strengthened the connection between the team and supporters since arriving at the club. More than 15,000 Palace supporters traveled to Leipzig to witness the historic occasion, with thousands more watching on a big screen at Selhurst Park.

Midfielder Adam Wharton was among those who trained before the match, though Glasner kept his team selection uncertain. Wharton's exclusion from England's World Cup squad by manager Thomas Tuchel had drawn attention, but he was available for selection for this crucial fixture.

Rayo Vallecano, managed by Iñigo Pérez, operated on a significantly smaller budget than Palace but competed earnestly throughout. The Spanish side, who finished eighth in La Liga, were unable to find an equalizer as Palace's defense remained solid.

Palace now face the challenge of appointing Glasner's successor. The club is hopeful of securing Andoni Iraola, the outgoing Bournemouth manager, though he has attracted interest from Milan and Bayer Leverkusen. Pierre Sage, who led Lens to second place in Ligue 1 this season, represents an alternative option.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested that a court reopen a lawsuit involving President Trump and the IRS.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed proper legal procedures by negotiating a settlement directly rather than allowing court oversight.

The settlement created a $1.776 billion fund designed to compensate individuals who claim the government wronged them. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented established legal processes that should have involved judicial review of the settlement terms.

cards.headline: Five Trapped in Flooded Laos Cave Found Alive After More Than a Week
cards.teaser: Rescuers located five of seven people who had been trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for more than a week, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Rescuers have discovered five villagers alive in a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week trapped underground. Video footage shows the men crouched together on a rocky ledge in a dark chamber, surrounded by muddy water. They had entered the cave on Wednesday before water levels rose, trapping them inside.

Two villagers remain missing as rescue teams continue their search through the narrow, water-filled passages. Rescuers have navigated the challenging conditions amid ongoing rain to reach the trapped group.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over $1.2 million in prediction market trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly used insider information to profit on Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Justice Department charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly used insider information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket bets. Prosecutors say Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential data about search-related trends in 2025 and placed wagers knowing the outcomes before the public did.

This is the second federal case targeting someone for using insider information on a prediction market platform. The charges show authorities are increasingly applying insider trading laws to newer financial platforms like Polymarket.

cards.headline: Trump administration considers halting international flight processing in sanctuary cities
cards.teaser: Homeland Security is drawing up plans to stop processing customs and immigration at airports in cities that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is developing plans to stop processing international flights at airports in sanctuary cities, according to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. He announced the proposal during a Fox News interview, saying the move would be in response to recent protests at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center in New Jersey.

Sanctuary cities are jurisdictions that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Major airports like Los Angeles International would be affected by the proposal, which would halt customs and immigration processing for arriving international travelers.

cards.headline: Amazon and Snowflake announce $6 billion cloud computing deal
cards.teaser: Snowflake agreed to spend $6 billion on Amazon cloud services for computing chips focused on agentic systems.
cards.body:
Snowflake has committed to a five-year agreement with Amazon Web Services to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing chips designed for artificial intelligence applications. The deal positions Amazon's custom processors as an alternative to Nvidia's offerings.

Snowflake's stock surged 36 percent following the announcement, which coincided with the company's earnings beat. The company also raised its sales outlook, citing strong demand for AI infrastructure investments as a key factor driving the partnership.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: The Justice Department charged a Google information security engineer with using inside information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google information security engineer Michele Spagnuolo with fraud for allegedly using confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket. He wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and netted approximately $1.2 million in profits.

Spagnuolo allegedly had access to Google's confidential data about search trends, giving him advance knowledge of outcomes before the trading public. The case marks one of the first major enforcement actions against insider trading on prediction market platforms, which allow users to bet on real-world events.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's motion to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency.
cards.body:
Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by California's civil rights enforcement agency has been rejected by the court. The decision allows the case to proceed past the dismissal phase.

California's civil rights agency expressed satisfaction with the court's ruling and indicated the case is expected to advance to trial in July.

cards.headline: Websites can track visitors by measuring SSD activity through browsers
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered a new privacy vulnerability that allows websites to monitor visitors by analyzing their solid-state drive activity using simple JavaScript.
cards.body:
Security researchers have identified a new method websites can use to track visitors by measuring solid-state drive activity patterns. The technique works through standard web browsers using basic JavaScript code without requiring special permissions or access.

The tracking method exploits telltale patterns in how SSDs read and write data. Websites can detect these patterns to create fingerprints of individual users or monitor their behavior. The discovery adds to growing concerns about web privacy and the ways sites can track users beyond traditional cookies.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into ticket pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup, with a specific focus on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The subpoena seeks information about how FIFA has managed ticket sales and pricing for the tournament.

The investigation centers on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations and allegations that FIFA's public messaging about tickets has contributed to inflated prices. The probe was announced by New York's Letitia James and New Jersey's Jennifer Davenport.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors to help resolve its conflict with Russia.

The request underscores Ukraine's continued need for advanced air defense systems as it faces ongoing Russian attacks.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government allowed people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet shutdown lasting nearly three months.
cards.body:
Iran ended an 88-day period of heavily censored news, television, and online communication, restoring some internet access to its citizens. The government had imposed a near-total internet shutdown that cut off most Iranians from global networks.

Not everyone in the country has regained access to the internet. Those who have reconnected are uncertain how long the restored service will last, given the government's control over digital infrastructure and history of imposing restrictions.

cards.headline: Lebanese Expect Prolonged Conflict Despite U.S.-Iran Diplomatic Efforts
cards.teaser: Residents of Lebanon say they do not believe diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran will bring peace as fighting intensifies in the country's south.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that diplomatic efforts will bring peace to their country. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon even as negotiations continue.

The escalating violence has left Lebanese residents resigned to a prolonged conflict. The fighting in the south persists despite ongoing talks aimed at establishing a broader cease-fire in the region.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she thought he might have been having a stroke and noted she had never seen him perform that way before or since.

The debate marked a significant moment in the 2024 presidential race, as Biden's halting delivery and confused moments during the event raised questions about his fitness for office and intensified scrutiny of his candidacy.

cards.headline: Stock indexes reach record highs as oil prices fall
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed at record levels as oil prices dropped amid diplomatic developments.
cards.body:
US stock indexes closed at record highs on Monday, buoyed by falling oil prices and optimism over potential peace negotiations between the US and Iran. Brent crude futures dropped 6% to $97.43 a barrel, marking the lowest level in two weeks as markets responded positively to signs of progress toward ending the three-month conflict.

The decline in oil prices provided broad support across the market, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reaching new peaks. Trump indicated that any agreement would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz, signaling momentum in the peace talks.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The administration has entered discussions about providing financial support to American drone companies.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is discussing potential government funding with US drone manufacturers to support domestic production and development. These conversations reflect efforts to strengthen American manufacturing capabilities in drone technology as foreign competitors have captured significant market share.

The funding discussions are part of a broader push to bolster domestic defense and aerospace capabilities across multiple sectors.

cards.headline: Google's AI search tool struggles to spell words correctly
cards.teaser: Google's artificial intelligence search feature has been producing errors when attempting to spell common words, including the company's own name.
cards.body:
Google's AI-powered search tool has encountered problems spelling basic words correctly. The system has struggled with terms like disregard, stop, and ignore, as well as the word Google itself. Multiple reports indicate the AI feature has felt worse to users recently.

Google released an update attempting to address the spelling issues. Users can now disable the AI-generated results in Google Search by using a simple search modifier. Some observers have questioned whether the problems could open the door for Microsoft to become a more viable search alternative.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell introduce bipartisan college sports reform bill
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have proposed legislation that would impose salary caps and transfer limits in college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell unveiled a bipartisan bill aimed at reforming college sports. The proposed legislation would establish salary caps for college athletes and place restrictions on player transfers between schools.

The bill includes provisions targeting coach poaching, a response to recent high-profile coaching moves in college sports. Arkansas basketball coach John Calipari expressed support for the legislation, which has been named the Protect College Sports Act. The measure represents an attempt by Congress to address ongoing disputes over compensation and mobility in collegiate athletics.

cards.headline: Tottenham close to signing Andy Robertson from Liverpool
cards.teaser: Tottenham are nearing an agreement to sign Scotland defender Andy Robertson following his departure from Liverpool.
cards.body: The move would see Robertson return to Premier League football with the north London club as they strengthen their defensive lineup.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses after French Open win in heat
cards.teaser: Czech player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open in Paris.
cards.body:
Czech player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match against Mariano Navone in a five-set thriller lasting over four and a half hours. He required a wheelchair to return to the locker room following the 6-3, 2-6, 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (11) victory. Mensik described the conditions as "insane," criticizing the lack of adequate cooling time during changeovers.

The incident has sparked calls for tournament reform. Mensik noted players get only 30 seconds to cool down during changeovers, insufficient for extreme heat conditions. Fellow player Novak Djokovic urged organizers to schedule more matches later in the day when temperatures are lower, emphasizing the need for common sense in tournament planning.

cards.headline: Spielberg Says AI Should Never Have Final Word on Creative Decisions in Hollywood
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against the use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he opposes AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood.

Spielberg said he thinks AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues. However, he drew a clear line when it comes to creative work in film. He stated that AI should never serve as the final word on anything creative.

The comments come as the entertainment industry grapples with how to use emerging AI technologies. Studios and production companies have explored using AI for various tasks, from scriptwriting assistance to visual effects work.

Spielberg did not specify which aspects of filmmaking he believes AI might assist with, if any. He focused his remarks on keeping human judgment central to creative decisions.

The director has helmed numerous acclaimed films over his decades-long career. His position on AI reflects broader concerns among creative professionals about automation replacing human artistry.

Other filmmakers and industry figures have weighed in on AI use in recent months. Some see potential benefits for technical tasks, while others worry about job losses and diminished creative quality.

Spielberg's comments on the podcast did not address ongoing labor discussions around AI protections. Writers and actors unions have sought contract language limiting AI use in their work.

The director emphasized that his opposition centers specifically on AI making final creative choices. He did not rule out all technological assistance in the filmmaking process.

His remarks add a prominent voice to the debate over AI in entertainment. As one of Hollywood's most successful directors, Spielberg's views carry weight in industry discussions about technology adoption.

The full podcast episode with Spielberg has not yet been released. Further details about his position on AI and other topics may emerge when the complete interview becomes available.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to criticism over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Senator Andy Kim defended his attendance at a protest outside a New Jersey migrant detention facility after facing criticism from Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.
cards.body:
Democratic Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin after the secretary criticized him for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in the state. During a cabinet meeting at the White House, Mullin said Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest.

Kim fired back at Mullin's remarks. The senator said the situation was never about him personally, pushing back against the characterization of his presence at the demonstration.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans endorse Paxton after divisive Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders moved to reconcile with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a $130 million primary battle against Senator John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are moving quickly to unite the party after a contentious Texas primary. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton by phone before publicly endorsing him on a radio show, signaling an effort to heal divisions within the party.

The endorsement reflects Republican concern about winning Texas in the general election. Party leaders are reassuring major donors that maintaining Senate control depends on success in the state. The goal is to move past the expensive and divisive primary race that saw Paxton defeat Senator John Cornyn.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his debate against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's 2024 presidential debate performance against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought Joe Biden might be having a stroke during the debate.

"I was frightened, because I had never, ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Jill Biden said in an interview set to air on Sunday. His faltering debate performance became a pivotal moment in the 2024 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after Texas Senate primary win
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are moving past tensions with Paxton following his victory over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas primary.
cards.body:
Republicans are working to mend relationships with Ken Paxton after the Texas attorney general won the Senate primary. Paxton defeated longtime incumbent John Cornyn in what observers described as a brutal primary contest.

The victory creates new dynamics within the Senate Republican caucus and raises concerns about fundraising capacity in Texas. Paxton's win also reflects tensions between President Trump and some Senate Republicans, as the race highlighted divisions within the party.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces backlash over first electric vehicle
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric car drew criticism in Italy and elsewhere, with investors selling shares and analysts questioning the model's appeal.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric model has sparked significant controversy following its unveiling. The car prompted mocking memes on social media and triggered a sharp decline in Ferrari's stock price as investors sold shares in response to the announcement.

The backlash reflects deeper concerns about the brand's future. A former Ferrari chairman cautioned that the shift to electric power risked "the destruction of a legend," while analysts questioned whether the model would resonate with Ferrari's traditional customer base. The reaction underscores the tension between the automotive industry's push toward electrification and concerns about preserving the performance characteristics that have long defined Ferrari.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: Electric vehicle maker Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as possibly the most important product the company has launched.

The R2 represents a significant expansion of Rivian's electric vehicle lineup beyond its initial offerings.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft photographed Mars during a recent flyby, producing detailed views of the planet's surface.
cards.body:
NASA released images of Mars captured by one of its spacecraft during a flyby of the red planet. The photographs show views of the Martian surface and features.

The images were taken as the spacecraft passed by Mars during its mission. NASA described the views as stunning, though the agency did not specify which spacecraft took the photographs or provide details about the flyby timing.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson discusses coaching change
cards.teaser: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said the team's coaching change feels like a breath of fresh air.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson spoke about the Ravens' recent coaching change, describing it as feeling like a breath of fresh air for the team. The quarterback also addressed his relationship with the organization, saying his commitment to the Ravens has not wavered.

Jackson declined to discuss details of ongoing contract negotiations with Baltimore. The quarterback said new coordinator Declan Doyle is making his job easier as the team adjusts to changes in the coaching staff.

cards.headline: Early Reactions Praise Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' as His Best Film in Two Decades
cards.teaser: First reactions to Steven Spielberg's science fiction film call it his strongest work in 20 years and highlight Emily Blunt's performance.
cards.body:
Early viewers of Steven Spielberg's science fiction film Disclosure Day praised it as his best work in 20 years. Reactions also highlighted Emily Blunt's performance, with some calling it an all-time achievement.

The film features Blunt in a leading role alongside Spielberg's direction. IMAX announced a live pre-show question and answer session with Spielberg and Blunt. A final trailer for the film was released, which includes footage of Spielberg himself.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Babydoll Dress Backlash
cards.teaser: The singer addressed criticism of her recent fashion choices, saying the reaction reflects normalized attitudes toward pedophilia.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo has addressed online criticism over her recent babydoll dress outfits, arguing that women shouldn't be held responsible for how others perceive their clothing choices. She contended that the backlash reflects how society normalizes pedophilia.

Internet commenters had accused her recent fashion selections of both infantilizing and sexualizing her. Rodrigo cited musicians Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love as inspiration for her style, defending her wardrobe decisions against the directed criticism.

cards.headline: Film 'Obsession' Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie saw its earnings rise in its second weekend, a pattern that has not occurred since Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
The film Obsession increased its box office earnings in its second weekend of release. This pattern has not been seen since the film Sound of Freedom, making it a notable achievement in theatrical performance.

The movie has emerged as a breakout box office hit this summer. Multiple outlets covered the unusual trajectory of the film's earnings and highlighted its photography work.

cards.headline: Court allows pro-Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals court judge permitted Mahmoud Khalil to stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court in his case against the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Judge Thomas Hardiman of the 3rd Circuit allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free as he takes his case to the Supreme Court. Hardiman, appointed by former President George W. Bush, put a hold on the circuit court's earlier ruling.

The prior ruling had determined that Khalil's case needed to meet certain legal requirements before proceeding. Khalil is challenging actions by the Trump administration, though the specific nature of his legal dispute was not detailed in available information.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Performing at Freedom 250 Concert Despite Being Listed
cards.teaser: The singer said he will not play the National Mall event despite organizers announcing him as a headliner for the patriotic celebration.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., despite organizers initially listing him as a headliner. Day stated the performance is "a no for me."

The Freedom 250 concert is part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. Other announced performers include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, C+C Music Factory, and Milli Vanilli. The event has drawn controversy.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos used his acceptance speech at the News Emmys to question the recent direction of the network.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior from District of Columbia International School, used his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys to challenge CBS News directly. He said the network's recent direction undermines the legacy of the legendary CBS journalist for whom the scholarship is named. Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award.

Campos's remarks gained attention for their boldness—criticizing the very organization honoring him. The timing coincided with broader concerns about editorial decisions at CBS News, including the shelving of investigative reporting.

hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Military Sites in Iran for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The U.S. military carried out strikes on military targets in southern Iran, marking the second such attack in three days as a fragile cease-fire remains under threat.

The strikes targeted a military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city in southern Iran, according to U.S. military officials. American forces also shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones and hit a drone ground-control station. A U.S. official said the attacks were conducted in self-defense.

Bandar Abbas sits along the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil shipments. The renewed military action sent oil prices higher as markets responded to fears of disruption in the strategic passage.

The strikes come as diplomatic efforts to establish a cease-fire hang in the balance. The U.S. and Iran have been engaged in negotiations, though the latest military exchange threatens to derail those talks. President Trump said Iran was "negotiating on fumes," suggesting the country's bargaining position has weakened.

The four attack drones destroyed by U.S. forces were launched by Iran before being intercepted. Officials characterized the drones and the ground-control station as imminent threats that justified the defensive strikes.

This marks an escalation in military tensions between the two countries over recent days. The previous U.S. strikes occurred just three days earlier, and officials have indicated that remaining military targets in Iran present more challenging and complicated scenarios for potential future action.

The cease-fire, described as fragile by multiple sources, now faces increased uncertainty following this second round of strikes. The military actions occurred even as diplomatic channels remained open between Washington and Tehran.

The situation in the Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern for international observers. Any prolonged disruption to shipping through the narrow passage could have significant implications for global energy markets and supply chains that depend on Middle Eastern oil exports.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases were reported in the capital Kampala.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak in the neighboring country intensifies. Suspected cases in the DRC have surpassed 900, with 119 suspected deaths reported, according to the country's ministry of communication. The World Health Organization has deemed the outbreak poses a "very high" risk for the DRC, though the risk of global spread remains low.

Seven confirmed cases of Ebola have been identified in Kampala, Uganda's capital. Ugandan health officials say the country has implemented robust disease surveillance systems to monitor and respond to the outbreak. International airlines have been instructed to follow safety protocols as the virus spreads in the region.

cards.headline: Five Trapped in Flooded Laos Cave Found Alive After More Than a Week
cards.teaser: Rescuers located five of seven people who had been trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for more than a week, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Rescuers have discovered five villagers alive in a flooded cave in Laos after more than a week trapped underground. Video footage shows the men crouched together on a rocky ledge in a dark chamber, surrounded by muddy water. They had entered the cave on Wednesday before water levels rose, trapping them inside.

Two villagers remain missing as rescue teams continue their search through the narrow, water-filled passages. Rescuers have navigated the challenging conditions amid ongoing rain to reach the trapped group.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government allowed people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet shutdown lasting nearly three months.
cards.body:
Iran ended an 88-day period of heavily censored news, television, and online communication, restoring some internet access to its citizens. The government had imposed a near-total internet shutdown that cut off most Iranians from global networks.

Not everyone in the country has regained access to the internet. Those who have reconnected are uncertain how long the restored service will last, given the government's control over digital infrastructure and history of imposing restrictions.

cards.headline: Lebanese Expect Prolonged Conflict Despite U.S.-Iran Diplomatic Efforts
cards.teaser: Residents of Lebanon say they do not believe diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran will bring peace as fighting intensifies in the country's south.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that diplomatic efforts will bring peace to their country. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon even as negotiations continue.

The escalating violence has left Lebanese residents resigned to a prolonged conflict. The fighting in the south persists despite ongoing talks aimed at establishing a broader cease-fire in the region.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his debate against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's 2024 presidential debate performance against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought Joe Biden might be having a stroke during the debate.

"I was frightened, because I had never, ever seen Joe like that before or since. Never," Jill Biden said in an interview set to air on Sunday. His faltering debate performance became a pivotal moment in the 2024 presidential campaign.

hero.headline: US strikes Iran military site, shoots down four drones
hero.body:
The US military launched strikes against a military facility in Bandar Abbas while also intercepting four Iranian attack drones during the operation, according to military statements.

Bandar Abbas, located on Iran's southern coast near the Strait of Hormuz, hosts significant Iranian naval operations and serves as a strategic port city. The US military confirmed the operation but provided limited details about the timing or specific targets involved.

The strikes occur as tensions between Washington and Tehran remain elevated. Negotiations are underway, with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi indicating that a counterproposal on nuclear matters could be ready within days. President Trump has set a 10 to 15-day deadline for Iran to reach a deal on its nuclear program, warning of "really bad things" if negotiations fail.

Trump indicated Friday that he is considering limited military strikes to pressure Iran into making concessions. "I guess I can say I am considering it," he told reporters when asked about a limited strike option. He added that Iran should "negotiate a fair deal."

The military buildup reflects heightened US activity in the region. Trump has ordered a massive increase in naval forces in the Middle East, including repositioning of aircraft carriers and other warships. According to US officials, military planning has advanced significantly, with options under consideration ranging from targeting specific individuals to pursuing leadership changes in Tehran.

Iran's nuclear program expanded after Trump withdrew from an international agreement during his first term. Israel led a military campaign against Iran in June 2025, which the US joined, though the campaign's long-term impact on Tehran's nuclear ambitions remains unclear.

Araghchi rejected the notion that military action can resolve Iran's nuclear program. "That has been tested last year. There were huge attacks on our facilities, they killed and assassinated our scientists, but they couldn't kill our nuclear programme," he said during discussions with Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Geneva this week.

During Geneva talks, both sides discussed principles for a potential agreement. Araghchi stated that discussions focused on ensuring "Iran's nuclear programme, including enrichment, is peaceful and would remain peaceful forever." He noted that Iran did not offer to suspend enrichment and the US did not demand zero enrichment.

A White House official responded by reiterating that "the president has been clear that Iran cannot have nuclear weapons or the capacity to build them, and that they cannot enrich uranium."

Trump also stated Saturday that a potential agreement would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's critical shipping chokepoints through which approximately one-fifth of global oil passes daily.

The UN has expressed concerns about heightened rhetoric and increased military activities in the region.

cards.headline: Paper mill disaster in Washington state may be deadliest industrial accident in modern state history
cards.teaser: Two people are confirmed dead and nine remain missing after a chemical vat ruptured at a Longview paper mill.
cards.body:
Two people have died and nine others are missing and presumed dead following a tank rupture at Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co in Longview on Tuesday morning. One person died after being transported to the hospital following the disaster.

Washington's governor has characterized the incident as potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. Fire department officials have shifted operations from rescue to recovery as they continue searching for the missing workers.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over $1.2 million in prediction market trades
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly used insider information to profit on Polymarket.
cards.body:
The Justice Department charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly used insider information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket bets. Prosecutors say Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential data about search-related trends in 2025 and placed wagers knowing the outcomes before the public did.

This is the second federal case targeting someone for using insider information on a prediction market platform. The charges show authorities are increasingly applying insider trading laws to newer financial platforms like Polymarket.

cards.headline: Trump administration considers halting international flight processing in sanctuary cities
cards.teaser: Homeland Security is drawing up plans to stop processing customs and immigration at airports in cities that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is developing plans to stop processing international flights at airports in sanctuary cities, according to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. He announced the proposal during a Fox News interview, saying the move would be in response to recent protests at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention center in New Jersey.

Sanctuary cities are jurisdictions that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Major airports like Los Angeles International would be affected by the proposal, which would halt customs and immigration processing for arriving international travelers.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she thought he might have been having a stroke and noted she had never seen him perform that way before or since.

The debate marked a significant moment in the 2024 presidential race, as Biden's halting delivery and confused moments during the event raised questions about his fitness for office and intensified scrutiny of his candidacy.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after Texas Senate primary win
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are moving past tensions with Paxton following his victory over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas primary.
cards.body:
Republicans are working to mend relationships with Ken Paxton after the Texas attorney general won the Senate primary. Paxton defeated longtime incumbent John Cornyn in what observers described as a brutal primary contest.

The victory creates new dynamics within the Senate Republican caucus and raises concerns about fundraising capacity in Texas. Paxton's win also reflects tensions between President Trump and some Senate Republicans, as the race highlighted divisions within the party.

hero.headline: Court orders customs chief to address tariff refund compliance
hero.body:
A court ordered the customs chief to appear at a hearing to address compliance with tariff refunds, signaling new concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay $166 billion owed from tariffs a court ruled were imposed illegally.

The demand for the customs chief to appear in person represented a departure from typical court proceedings and suggested judicial frustration with the pace or completeness of the refund process. The full $166 billion figure represents tariffs collected under policies that courts determined violated legal requirements.

The hearing will focus on whether the administration has taken adequate steps to comply with court orders requiring the tariffs to be refunded. The timeline for repayment and the mechanisms being used to return the funds to affected parties remain under judicial scrutiny.

The case centers on tariffs the Trump administration collected but that courts later found to be illegally imposed. The $166 billion total reflects the cumulative amount collected under those policies before courts invalidated them.

Judges typically do not require cabinet-level officials or agency heads to appear personally unless standard compliance mechanisms have failed or proven inadequate. The order for the customs chief to attend the hearing indicates the court may view current efforts as insufficient.

The refund process involves identifying who paid the tariffs, calculating refund amounts, and distributing payments. Delays or complications in any of these steps could trigger the kind of judicial intervention represented by this hearing order.

The appearance requirement puts direct pressure on the administration to demonstrate concrete progress on refunds. Courts have broad authority to enforce their orders, including through contempt findings or additional remedial measures if compliance remains lacking.

The customs chief will need to provide the court with detailed information about refund status, including how many claims have been processed, how much money has been returned, and what obstacles have slowed the process. The hearing represents a significant escalation in judicial oversight of the refund effort.

cards.headline: Amazon and Snowflake announce $6 billion cloud computing deal
cards.teaser: Snowflake agreed to spend $6 billion on Amazon cloud services for computing chips focused on agentic systems.
cards.body:
Snowflake has committed to a five-year agreement with Amazon Web Services to purchase $6 billion in cloud computing chips designed for artificial intelligence applications. The deal positions Amazon's custom processors as an alternative to Nvidia's offerings.

Snowflake's stock surged 36 percent following the announcement, which coincided with the company's earnings beat. The company also raised its sales outlook, citing strong demand for AI infrastructure investments as a key factor driving the partnership.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: The Justice Department charged a Google information security engineer with using inside information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google information security engineer Michele Spagnuolo with fraud for allegedly using confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket. He wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and netted approximately $1.2 million in profits.

Spagnuolo allegedly had access to Google's confidential data about search trends, giving him advance knowledge of outcomes before the trading public. The case marks one of the first major enforcement actions against insider trading on prediction market platforms, which allow users to bet on real-world events.

cards.headline: Stock indexes reach record highs as oil prices fall
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all closed at record levels as oil prices dropped amid diplomatic developments.
cards.body:
US stock indexes closed at record highs on Monday, buoyed by falling oil prices and optimism over potential peace negotiations between the US and Iran. Brent crude futures dropped 6% to $97.43 a barrel, marking the lowest level in two weeks as markets responded positively to signs of progress toward ending the three-month conflict.

The decline in oil prices provided broad support across the market, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all reaching new peaks. Trump indicated that any agreement would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz, signaling momentum in the peace talks.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces backlash over first electric vehicle
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric car drew criticism in Italy and elsewhere, with investors selling shares and analysts questioning the model's appeal.
cards.body:
Ferrari's new Luce electric model has sparked significant controversy following its unveiling. The car prompted mocking memes on social media and triggered a sharp decline in Ferrari's stock price as investors sold shares in response to the announcement.

The backlash reflects deeper concerns about the brand's future. A former Ferrari chairman cautioned that the shift to electric power risked "the destruction of a legend," while analysts questioned whether the model would resonate with Ferrari's traditional customer base. The reaction underscores the tension between the automotive industry's push toward electrification and concerns about preserving the performance characteristics that have long defined Ferrari.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The administration has entered discussions about providing financial support to American drone companies.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is discussing potential government funding with US drone manufacturers to support domestic production and development. These conversations reflect efforts to strengthen American manufacturing capabilities in drone technology as foreign competitors have captured significant market share.

The funding discussions are part of a broader push to bolster domestic defense and aerospace capabilities across multiple sectors.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million Polymarket profit
hero.body:
Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million betting on Polymarket. The engineer placed wagers totaling over $2.7 million on outcomes related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, according to the complaint.

The charges involve bets the engineer placed using knowledge he gained through his position at the company. Polymarket is a prediction market platform where users bet on the outcomes of real-world events. The platform has grown in popularity for wagering on everything from election results to corporate announcements.

The case marks a new frontier in insider trading enforcement, extending traditional securities law to prediction markets. Prosecutors allege the engineer used confidential information about Google's annual Year in Search campaign to place profitable bets on related outcomes before the information became public.

The Year in Search campaign is Google's annual roundup of the most popular search queries and trends. The timing and content of the campaign could provide betting advantages to someone with advance knowledge of the results or announcement details.

The engineer risked a total of $2.7 million across multiple wagers, ultimately profiting $1.2 million from the trades. The complaint does not specify how many individual bets were placed or over what time period.

Insider trading laws traditionally apply to securities like stocks and bonds, but prosecutors have increasingly applied them to other markets where material nonpublic information could provide an unfair advantage. Prediction markets have faced regulatory scrutiny over whether they constitute illegal gambling or unregulated securities trading.

Polymarket operates using cryptocurrency and has attracted millions in trading volume on high-profile events. The platform faced regulatory action from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in 2022 but continued operating with restrictions on U.S. users.

The charges could set precedent for how insider trading laws apply to prediction markets and what types of corporate information are protected. Google has not commented on the case or the engineer's employment status.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's motion to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency.
cards.body:
Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by California's civil rights enforcement agency has been rejected by the court. The decision allows the case to proceed past the dismissal phase.

California's civil rights agency expressed satisfaction with the court's ruling and indicated the case is expected to advance to trial in July.

cards.headline: Websites can track visitors by measuring SSD activity through browsers
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered a new privacy vulnerability that allows websites to monitor visitors by analyzing their solid-state drive activity using simple JavaScript.
cards.body:
Security researchers have identified a new method websites can use to track visitors by measuring solid-state drive activity patterns. The technique works through standard web browsers using basic JavaScript code without requiring special permissions or access.

The tracking method exploits telltale patterns in how SSDs read and write data. Websites can detect these patterns to create fingerprints of individual users or monitor their behavior. The discovery adds to growing concerns about web privacy and the ways sites can track users beyond traditional cookies.

cards.headline: Google's AI search tool struggles to spell words correctly
cards.teaser: Google's artificial intelligence search feature has been producing errors when attempting to spell common words, including the company's own name.
cards.body:
Google's AI-powered search tool has encountered problems spelling basic words correctly. The system has struggled with terms like disregard, stop, and ignore, as well as the word Google itself. Multiple reports indicate the AI feature has felt worse to users recently.

Google released an update attempting to address the spelling issues. Users can now disable the AI-generated results in Google Search by using a simple search modifier. Some observers have questioned whether the problems could open the door for Microsoft to become a more viable search alternative.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: Electric vehicle maker Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as possibly the most important product the company has launched.

The R2 represents a significant expansion of Rivian's electric vehicle lineup beyond its initial offerings.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft photographed Mars during a recent flyby, producing detailed views of the planet's surface.
cards.body:
NASA released images of Mars captured by one of its spacecraft during a flyby of the red planet. The photographs show views of the Martian surface and features.

The images were taken as the spacecraft passed by Mars during its mission. NASA described the views as stunning, though the agency did not specify which spacecraft took the photographs or provide details about the flyby timing.

hero.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League in Glasner's final match
hero.body:
Crystal Palace secured their first major European trophy by defeating Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in the second half, delivering Oliver Glasner a perfect send-off in his last match as manager.

The victory proved especially significant for Palace, who had been denied a place in this season's Europa League despite winning the FA Cup last year. UEFA had ruled that John Textor held a controlling interest in both Palace and Lyon, breaching multi-club ownership regulations. By winning the Conference League, Palace have secured the Europa League spot that should have been theirs.

Glasner's departure marks the end of a remarkable 12-month period in which he has won three trophies with the club. Along with the Conference League title, he guided Palace to both the FA Cup and Community Shield. The Austrian also won the Europa League with Eintracht Frankfurt in 2022, cementing his status as one of the club's greatest managers.

Before the final, Glasner addressed his players after they held a farewell party for him. He explained his hope that winning would allow them to experience European football at the level they deserved. "The best thing would be winning tomorrow because then the players would be in the Europa League next year and then we get what we should have got this year," Glasner said. He expressed his wish to watch them compete in the Europa League next season, confident they could succeed there too.

Club captain Dean Henderson praised Glasner's impact, describing his departure as "a huge miss." The goalkeeper noted that the manager had strengthened the connection between the team and supporters since arriving at the club. More than 15,000 Palace supporters traveled to Leipzig to witness the historic occasion, with thousands more watching on a big screen at Selhurst Park.

Midfielder Adam Wharton was among those who trained before the match, though Glasner kept his team selection uncertain. Wharton's exclusion from England's World Cup squad by manager Thomas Tuchel had drawn attention, but he was available for selection for this crucial fixture.

Rayo Vallecano, managed by Iñigo Pérez, operated on a significantly smaller budget than Palace but competed earnestly throughout. The Spanish side, who finished eighth in La Liga, were unable to find an equalizer as Palace's defense remained solid.

Palace now face the challenge of appointing Glasner's successor. The club is hopeful of securing Andoni Iraola, the outgoing Bournemouth manager, though he has attracted interest from Milan and Bayer Leverkusen. Pierre Sage, who led Lens to second place in Ligue 1 this season, represents an alternative option.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket prices
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into ticket pricing for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup, with a specific focus on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The subpoena seeks information about how FIFA has managed ticket sales and pricing for the tournament.

The investigation centers on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations and allegations that FIFA's public messaging about tickets has contributed to inflated prices. The probe was announced by New York's Letitia James and New Jersey's Jennifer Davenport.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell introduce bipartisan college sports reform bill
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have proposed legislation that would impose salary caps and transfer limits in college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell unveiled a bipartisan bill aimed at reforming college sports. The proposed legislation would establish salary caps for college athletes and place restrictions on player transfers between schools.

The bill includes provisions targeting coach poaching, a response to recent high-profile coaching moves in college sports. Arkansas basketball coach John Calipari expressed support for the legislation, which has been named the Protect College Sports Act. The measure represents an attempt by Congress to address ongoing disputes over compensation and mobility in collegiate athletics.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson discusses coaching change
cards.teaser: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said the team's coaching change feels like a breath of fresh air.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson spoke about the Ravens' recent coaching change, describing it as feeling like a breath of fresh air for the team. The quarterback also addressed his relationship with the organization, saying his commitment to the Ravens has not wavered.

Jackson declined to discuss details of ongoing contract negotiations with Baltimore. The quarterback said new coordinator Declan Doyle is making his job easier as the team adjusts to changes in the coaching staff.

cards.headline: Tottenham close to signing Andy Robertson from Liverpool
cards.teaser: Tottenham are nearing an agreement to sign Scotland defender Andy Robertson following his departure from Liverpool.
cards.body: The move would see Robertson return to Premier League football with the north London club as they strengthen their defensive lineup.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses after French Open win in heat
cards.teaser: Czech player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open in Paris.
cards.body:
Czech player Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match against Mariano Navone in a five-set thriller lasting over four and a half hours. He required a wheelchair to return to the locker room following the 6-3, 2-6, 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (11) victory. Mensik described the conditions as "insane," criticizing the lack of adequate cooling time during changeovers.

The incident has sparked calls for tournament reform. Mensik noted players get only 30 seconds to cool down during changeovers, insufficient for extreme heat conditions. Fellow player Novak Djokovic urged organizers to schedule more matches later in the day when temperatures are lower, emphasizing the need for common sense in tournament planning.

hero.headline: Spielberg Says AI Should Never Have Final Word on Creative Decisions in Hollywood
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against the use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he opposes AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood.

Spielberg said he thinks AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues. However, he drew a clear line when it comes to creative work in film. He stated that AI should never serve as the final word on anything creative.

The comments come as the entertainment industry grapples with how to use emerging AI technologies. Studios and production companies have explored using AI for various tasks, from scriptwriting assistance to visual effects work.

Spielberg did not specify which aspects of filmmaking he believes AI might assist with, if any. He focused his remarks on keeping human judgment central to creative decisions.

The director has helmed numerous acclaimed films over his decades-long career. His position on AI reflects broader concerns among creative professionals about automation replacing human artistry.

Other filmmakers and industry figures have weighed in on AI use in recent months. Some see potential benefits for technical tasks, while others worry about job losses and diminished creative quality.

Spielberg's comments on the podcast did not address ongoing labor discussions around AI protections. Writers and actors unions have sought contract language limiting AI use in their work.

The director emphasized that his opposition centers specifically on AI making final creative choices. He did not rule out all technological assistance in the filmmaking process.

His remarks add a prominent voice to the debate over AI in entertainment. As one of Hollywood's most successful directors, Spielberg's views carry weight in industry discussions about technology adoption.

The full podcast episode with Spielberg has not yet been released. Further details about his position on AI and other topics may emerge when the complete interview becomes available.

cards.headline: Early Reactions Praise Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day' as His Best Film in Two Decades
cards.teaser: First reactions to Steven Spielberg's science fiction film call it his strongest work in 20 years and highlight Emily Blunt's performance.
cards.body:
Early viewers of Steven Spielberg's science fiction film Disclosure Day praised it as his best work in 20 years. Reactions also highlighted Emily Blunt's performance, with some calling it an all-time achievement.

The film features Blunt in a leading role alongside Spielberg's direction. IMAX announced a live pre-show question and answer session with Spielberg and Blunt. A final trailer for the film was released, which includes footage of Spielberg himself.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Babydoll Dress Backlash
cards.teaser: The singer addressed criticism of her recent fashion choices, saying the reaction reflects normalized attitudes toward pedophilia.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo has addressed online criticism over her recent babydoll dress outfits, arguing that women shouldn't be held responsible for how others perceive their clothing choices. She contended that the backlash reflects how society normalizes pedophilia.

Internet commenters had accused her recent fashion selections of both infantilizing and sexualizing her. Rodrigo cited musicians Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love as inspiration for her style, defending her wardrobe decisions against the directed criticism.

cards.headline: Film 'Obsession' Posts Rare Second-Weekend Box Office Increase
cards.teaser: The movie saw its earnings rise in its second weekend, a pattern that has not occurred since Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
The film Obsession increased its box office earnings in its second weekend of release. This pattern has not been seen since the film Sound of Freedom, making it a notable achievement in theatrical performance.

The movie has emerged as a breakout box office hit this summer. Multiple outlets covered the unusual trajectory of the film's earnings and highlighted its photography work.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Performing at Freedom 250 Concert Despite Being Listed
cards.teaser: The singer said he will not play the National Mall event despite organizers announcing him as a headliner for the patriotic celebration.
cards.body:
